Camila — quick sizing notes after scanning the CSV and histograms:

1) Baseline compute: /generate-chat baseline 8 qps -> with average response ~120 tokens and streaming overhead we'd need roughly 1 x A10G-equivalent slot per ~10 sustained qps for latency p95 ~250ms. So baseline: 1-2 A10G equivalents to cover steady-state.

2) Burst handling: p99 spikes to 110 qps with microbursts 2–4 minutes. Recommend a burst pool + autoscale that can add ~6 additional A10G-equivalents transiently. For cost savings consider a small reserved pool (2 reserved GPUs) + transient burst capacity on demand.

3) Memory/KV cache: long responses (p99 1200 tokens) increase KV cache per session. For 4–8k concurrent sessions (per Camila note), plan for ~48–96 GB of KV cache memory across the pool — this maps to using GPUs with larger VRAM (80GB-class) or distributing session state across shards. If sessions are sticky, use session pinning to reduce cross-host KV retrieval.

4) Oversubscription guidance: safe oversubscription for non-streaming routes (embeddings/rerank) up to 2x. For streaming chat, keep near 1.1–1.2x to avoid latency tail spikes.

5) Model fallback policy: use a cheaper variant for overflow (e.g., quantized 8-bit) for up to 10% traffic as they tolerate quality drop. Route based on p95 latency in the last 60s.

Next steps: I can turn this into a short capacity sketch (1-pager) with GPU sku mapping and estimated monthly cost. Anything else I should call out for the Friday call?
